content.text: {"headline":"Approve P1: no-cost break shift, general callback and one evening cross-skill move lifts service level to 83.7% for 15:00-20:00, with payments back above the 80% target.","why":"The problem is fewer agents, not more calls: payments has 13 absences against a usual 2.6 and general has 15 against 2.4, mostly 'Unplanned leave - family function'. Volume and handle time are close to plan. Doing nothing gives 81.3% overall, but payments drops to 77.8%, below the 80% target. P1 delays 15:00-16:00 breaks on both queues by 45 minutes, runs IVR callback on general 15:00-16:00, and moves 1 cross-skilled agent from general to payments 19:00-20:00. That brings payments to 82.0% and keeps general at 86.2%, with abandons falling from 4.6% to 3.9%. It costs nothing and breaks no policy. It is the cheapest plan that hits target on both queues.","trade_offs":["Payments has the least headroom: 82.0% against the 80% target. P2 gives 86.5% on payments and 86.9% overall for INR 906, but it cancels coaching and pushes 20% of payments status/refund contacts to chat.","P3 (INR 1,098) and P4 (INR 1,350) add only small further gains: 87.2% and 87.7% overall, with abandons at 3.5% and 3.3%. They rely on chat deflection, a 2-agent move or overtime.","Risk to general is minimal. It goes from 86.3% to 86.2% under P1 despite giving up 1 agent 19:00-20:00. General callers in 15:00-16:00 will be offered callbacks instead of waiting.","Delayed breaks put more strain on agents who are already covering for absent colleagues."],"watch":"Watch payments service level, especially into the evening. Its margin is only 2 points above target. If it slips toward 80%, or more absences come in, move up to P2 (INR 906). No escalation to the duty manager is needed."}
